name: machine-watch
description: Deterministic scheduled watcher: a machine gate polls a check command at a fixed cadence and costs ZERO tokens while parked; the run releases only when the check exits 0. LAUNCH LAW (the whole point): always launch with run args lane_key=<team>/<watch-name> — a second dispatch while the incumbent is unfinished is DEDUPED by the engine (no spawn; the incumbent's run_id comes back), so cron double-fire cannot double-run the watch. Seeds (run_context map, ALL required): 'watch_name' = human label echoed into the report; 'check_cmd' = one shell line whose exit 0 means the watched condition is clear (e.g. 'test -f /ready.flag && pgrep -f worker >/dev/null'). The bootstrap node writes check_cmd verbatim to $HERMES_HOME/machine-watch-example/check_cmd.txt; the gate polls that file through a fixed probe — edit the file to retarget the watch without touching the graph. This gate has no human question: a machine wait polls only the check. Exit 0 releases; exit 1 parks as unhealthy; exit 2 parks as broken, writes a sticky probe_broken diagnostic until a genuine healthy poll, and never treats a blank command as health. The 300-second deadline fails loudly. A later dispatch of a completed lane_key is a NEW run, not a deduped retry; a scheduler that knows health is unchanged should skip dispatch while transition.claim exists; otherwise this gate parks the duplicate until bounded timeout. Human escalation belongs outside this gate. Scratch root $HERMES_HOME/machine-watch-example is shared handoff state: one watch per root, or change both the bootstrap goal and the probe path together. every_s/timeout_s set poll cadence and bounded wait; choose >=30s polling for production. Keep the scratch root stable across dispatches: transition.claim is a durable at-most-once reservation written by the gate; delivered.transition is a separate acknowledgement written only after actual receiver acceptance. An observed exit-1 check re-arms the claim; exit-2 never re-arms. On a repeated healthy dispatch the gate parks rather than running report again. A scheduler may skip that duplicate only when it independently knows health has not changed; otherwise dispatch so the gate can observe an exit-1 re-arm. For a new watch use a distinct scratch root and lane_key. The report must acknowledge only after the receiver accepts the delivery; its fenced answer alone is not proof of an external notification.

until_argv:
import os, pathlib, subprocess, sys
S=pathlib.Path(os.environ.get('MW_STATE_ROOT') or (os.environ.get('HERMES_HOME') or '~/.hermes') + '/machine-watch-example').expanduser()
C=S/'check_cmd.txt'
B=S/'probe_broken'
L=S/'last_probe.json'
A=S/'transition.claim'
D=S/'delivered.transition'
def broken(why):
    B.write_text(why+'\n')
    print('machine-watch probe broken: '+why, file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)
try:
    cmd=C.read_text().strip()
except OSError as e:
    broken('missing or unreadable handoff: '+str(e))
if not cmd:
    broken('empty check command')
try:
    rc=subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True).returncode
except OSError as e:
    broken('adapter could not run: '+str(e))
L.write_text(str(rc))
if rc==0:
    B.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    if A.exists():
        print('machine-watch: transition already claimed; waiting for unhealthy re-arm', file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    A.write_text('healthy claimed\n')
    sys.exit(0)
if rc!=1:
    broken('adapter exit '+str(rc))
A.unlink(missing_ok=True)
D.unlink(missing_ok=True)
sys.exit(1)

nodes.goal:
The machine gate 'watch' released when the polled check exited 0 (its committed answer in ## Inputs carries attempt + waited_s + last_exit). Read $HERMES_HOME/machine-watch-example/last_probe.json. For the watch named in the bootstrap payload, reply with ONLY fenced json {"released": true, "attempts": <int from the gate answer>, "waited_s": <int from the gate answer>, "report": "<one line: watch_name cleared after N polls, last probe exit E>"}
Deliver the transition to the receiver at most once. The gate wrote $HERMES_HOME/machine-watch-example/transition.claim before releasing, so a repeated completed dispatch with unchanged health parks without starting another report. After the receiver actually accepts the report, write $HERMES_HOME/machine-watch-example/delivered.transition with watch_name and last probe exit 0 as the delivery acknowledgement. If delivery fails, reply released:false and do not acknowledge; leave the claim in place to prevent an uncertain duplicate. An operator may clear an undelivered claim ONLY after establishing no delivery occurred. A real exit-1 poll re-arms the claim; exit-2 never re-arms.
